title: The Man Who Missed His Train
text:
Last Tuesday I was late for my train. I ran to the station, but the train left two minutes before I arrived. I was angry with myself because I woke up early that day.

The next train was in one hour, so I bought a coffee and sat on a bench. An old man sat next to me and started talking about his garden. He told me about his tomatoes for twenty minutes.

At first I was not interested. Then I noticed something: he was happy. He had a small garden and it was enough for him. When my train came, I felt calmer than before. Sometimes being late gives you something you did not plan.

title: Learning in the Kitchen
text:
My friend Anna wanted to learn English, but she never had time. She worked all day and studied nothing in the evening. Then she found a simple idea.

She started to watch cooking videos in English while she made dinner. She did not understand everything, but she understood the important words: cut, add, mix, wait. Every evening she heard the same words again.

After three months something changed. She listened to a podcast in the car and understood half of it. She was surprised. She did not study grammar, but her ears got used to the language. Now she says that the kitchen was her first classroom.

title: The Rule of Two Minutes
text:
I read about a simple rule and decided to try it for one month. The rule says: if a task takes less than two minutes, do it now.

In the first week it was strange. I washed my cup immediately after coffee. I answered short messages at once. I put my clothes in the wardrobe instead of on the chair.

After two weeks my flat was cleaner and my head was quieter. Small tasks did not wait for me anymore. The rule is not magic, of course. Big projects still need real time and real energy. But the small things stopped growing into a mountain.
